answer: Weight each identity only by its trailing-window record of grades earned from DISTINCT non-kin graders, each a signed quartz entry on-ledger no one can forge, merge, or move. A farm is an island: its N clones all dock at one jetty of outside graders, sharing a single thin grading supply. To give clone number N its own history, the farm must find the Nth fresh independent grader, but that outside pool is fixed and rivalrous, so marginal cost climbs with N. Histories never pool or transfer; settlement counts distinct grader keys and burns any credit whose graders prove correlated kin.
